learning_objective: 🎯 Master the rules, court dimensions, fundamental skills, and terminology of major individual sports such as Athletics, Badminton, Table Tennis, and Gymnastics!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Athletics comprises sprints, middle/long-distance races, jumping events (long jump, high jump), and throwing events (shot put, javelin, discus), each governed by precise track measurements and foul rules.
Key skills include the high clear, drop shot, net shot, and powerful smash. The game requires agility, wrist snap, and tactical court positioning.
Played on a regulation table using specialized grips (shakehand or penhold), focusing on topspin, backspin, footwork, and rapid reaction times.
A sport testing flexibility, balance, strength, and grace across apparatuses like the floor exercise, balance beam, parallel bars, and vault.

fun_activity.title: 🏸 Wrist Snap Practice
fun_activity.instructions: Hold a badminton racket (or a rolled-up newspaper) and practice flicking your wrist forward and backward without moving your arm from the elbow. Notice how wrist speed generates power for a smash!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize standard court dimensions and net heights for Badminton and Table Tennis.
📌 In Athletics, be ready to draw a diagram of a standard 400m track or explain the phase sequence of a Long Jump (Approach, Take-off, Flight, Landing).
📌 Know the difference between track events (running) and field events (jumping and throwing).
quick_recap: ⭐ A standard athletics running track is 400 meters in circumference.
⭐ In Badminton, a match is normally played as the best of 3 games of 21 points each.
⭐ Gymnastics requires extreme neuromuscular coordination, flexibility, and core strength.
